steps.claim: The note states obligation 3 per-operation: 'each retained operation must have the same full-domain effect on the remaining joint state', and motivates it with a single read of G observing a different intermediate version. Read as operators the sentence is vacuous (same CX unitary in both traces, which would admit yak scratch-read); read in-context it rejects any retained read whose observed intermediate value changes, even if a later retained operation cancels the difference. The note's own executed check is the overall truth table, so the text and the oracle define different rules.

Differing input: source tail 'cx z d; cx d y; cx d y; cx x d; qfree d' after the common 'd=qalloc; cx x d; cx z d' (i.e. scratch-read with the read duplicated). At x=1,z=1 the first retained cx d y has in-context effect y ^= x in the source but y ^= x XOR z in the recompute candidate, so the per-operation rule refuses; yet the two reads cancel and independent execution of both literal traces on all 8 bases gives identical interfaces with all releases clean, so the composed ISA condition admits this recompute.
steps.by: witness:.tmp/e9a-council/muse/probe.py (independent executor; PROBE-A double-read: overall diff 0, dirty 0, per-op first-read effect differs when z=1)

blocking.problem: ASSUMED: §6.2 as quoted lists window-closing events disjunctively: 'a non-diagonal gate on a wire in S or in g' (clause 1) and separately 'a permutation change to a wire in S not undone before g's cleanup' (clause 4). Read literally, clause 1 already includes the permutation X on a wire of S, so the tdf/w2b flip would close the window at the first X and the 'undone' definition could never apply. The intended reading (clause 1 means a non-permutation non-diagonal gate) is recoverable only from §6.1's provenance table, which gives permutation gates their own row distinct from the 'non-diagonal gate on u' row; §6.2 itself never says this. The note adopts the intended reading silently - correctly, since the estimator and reviews r3/r4 treat the tdf source as valid - but a reader of §6.2 alone can derive the opposite verdict for tdf/w2b. This is a spec-wording gap for the spec owner, not an editor error, and per the rubric does not count against accept.
blocking.fix: Spec owner: in §6.2 clause 1, write 'a non-diagonal, non-permutation gate on a wire in S or in g (permutation changes to S are clause 4)'. Note editor (one line in §3.1): name the adopted reading and cite the §6.1 table rows that force it.

summary: The note is the first of five rounds to decide all six witnesses correctly for the right reasons: every quotation is verbatim from ISA 0.9 at the gate-pinned hash (verified mechanically), obligations 1-2 and §3.1 basis preservation follow §5.3/§6.2/K81 exactly, the two refusals refuse only the recompute (both sources stay valid under reverse, so no north-star narrowing), and the evidence is genuinely executable - I re-ran the witness suite (6 passed, 4 ignored; the ignored four fail on today's generic pending path exactly as §5 claims), re-executed all fixtures in an independent interpreter with identical counts, and reproduced the hand-derived resource totals by running the estimator on the literal candidate traces. It is not yet acceptable as a definition to implement from, for one reason: obligation 3 is written per-operation while the spec's condition (§6.1) and the note's own oracle are composed/overall, and the two readings disagree on a concrete double-read variant of scratch-read that the ISA admits (B1, with executed witness) - precisely the over-narrow predicate shape that sank rounds r1/r3/r4. Restating that one obligation in composed form and pinning it with a seventh witness is the whole path to accept; B2 (a §6.2 clause-1 wording ambiguity the note reads correctly but silently) is a spec-gap for the spec owner and does not count against accept.
